title: ARPAPED Verification Record
description: Machine-readable record of the mandatory Verify phase. Written into the resulting state; the next cycle re-runs the harness and accepts no goal until the record is green.

harness.description: Path or identity of the verification harness in the resulting state.

environment.description: The platform this harness run actually executed on -- captured ONCE per verification run (constant for the whole run, never per-check, since the OS/arch/runtime don't change mid-run) so a platform-specific failure (e.g. a Windows-only pipe-buffering bug, observed for real) is diagnosable from the record alone, never requiring an after-the-fact 'what OS was this run on?'.

os.description: e.g. 'Windows', 'Linux', 'Darwin' (Python's platform.system(), or the equivalent for whatever language the harness runs in).

runtime.description: e.g. 'CPython 3.9.6', 'Node 20.11.0' -- language-agnostic, whatever runtime actually executed this harness, never assumed to be Python.

check_id.description: Unique across the entire record so an audit can reference exactly one check.

input.description: The actual input this check's capability operation was called with -- what produced the recorded trace/selection/evidence/expected/actual. Any JSON type, matching whatever the operation's own contract-declared input shape is. Without this, a check's observations are unreproducible from the record alone: reconstructing 'what call produced this trace' would require re-reading the harness's own source rather than the record it wrote.

check_type.description: Optional classifier. When set to 'capability_operation', the check MUST carry an observed 'trace' (see the conditional below) equal to the Bridge's own response.trace.

observed.description: Observed evidence (state, counts, message). Always present for failed checks; may also be recorded for passed checks.

trace.description: The OBSERVED full Bridge trace (the Bridge's own response.trace) for this capability operation, evaluated as validated -> discovered -> policy_evaluated -> selected -> executed. REQUIRED for every capability-operation check; must be copied from the Bridge, never constructed by the harness (R8, Gate 28).

regression_for.description: Previous defect id this check protects against, when applicable.

expected.description: The value this check asserted against, structured rather than interpolated into a string (contrast the older pattern of writing 'observed': "expected X, got Y"). Any JSON type -- a trace array, a response.output object, an implementation_id string, a scalar count. Present together with 'actual' or not at all (see dependentRequired below) -- 'observed' remains the right field for a check with no natural expected/actual split (e.g. contract/manifest schema validation).

actual.description: The value actually observed for this check, structured the same way as 'expected'. A lone 'actual' with no stated 'expected' is not a comparison; a lone 'expected' proves nothing was actually observed -- both or neither.

selection.description: Bridge-level Decision Context for this check's capability operation -- distinct from the agent-level Phase-4 decisions[] in agent-cycle-report.schema.json (2-RULES.md glossary). Copied from the Bridge's own observed response.selection, never invented -- the same authenticity 'trace' already requires (R8, Gate 28/37).

candidates.description: Every candidate discovered AND policy-allowed for this request (the Bridge's own post-policy_evaluated, pre-selected list). A single-candidate array is honest and expected when only one implementation exists or is policy-allowed for this request -- it is not evidence of a bug.

reason.description: Deterministic, honest wording, e.g. "highest priority (200) among 2 policy-allowed candidates", or, after a failover, "priority 150 selected after console.write.v2 failed over, among 2 policy-allowed candidates". Never a vague 'best match'.

evidence.description: Process-kind (executor_kind: process) execution evidence -- populated only when the selected implementation ran out-of-process (R4 Worker). Absent for direct/factory/remote-kind operations: there is nothing analogous to capture for an in-process call sharing the Bridge's own stdout, or a Remote call whose own runtime already records its own genuine trace.

response_output.description: The structured {'output': {...}} payload the worker actually returned over process-executor-protocol.schema.json for this call -- already produced in memory today, persisted here rather than discarded.

stdout.description: Raw bytes (UTF-8, errors='replace') the worker wrote to its own OS-level stdout during the span this invocation exclusively held its worker connection. Genuinely empty for an implementation whose responsibility never prints (e.g. greeting.compose.process, which only makes a nested Bridge call) and genuinely non-empty for one whose responsibility IS to print (e.g. console.write.process) -- never assumed empty.

stderr.description: Same capture, for the worker's own stderr, over the same invocation span.

worker_alive.description: Whether the worker's TCP connection was still usable immediately after this call.

process_exit_code.description: A non-blocking Popen.poll() snapshot taken right after this call -- null while the pooled worker is still running (the normal case), an integer only if it had already exited/crashed. Not 'the' exit code of one request -- a pooled process outlives any single call.
